The **ADHD-udredningsforløb** (ADHD diagnostic assessment process) is the clinical procedure used to investigate whether a child or young person has ADHD. This process is a fundamental component of the Danish healthcare system's quality assurance, as it is central to both registration in the ADHD Database (ADHD-DATABASEN) and the calculation of national quality indicators [^src1]. Because the assessment process directly impacts national quality metrics, there is ongoing work to revise the indicator set so that it better reflects actual clinical practice and provides a more accurate measurement of quality [^src2].

A key administrative and procedural aspect of the ADHD-udredningsforløb involves cases where the initial suspicion of ADHD is not confirmed. If a clinical assessment is stopped within 90 days because the suspicion is disproven, the case can be excluded from the database's assessment population. To achieve this, healthcare providers must report the specific process marker [[agx01b|AGX01B]] ("ADHD-udredning slut, mistanke afkræftet" / "ADHD assessment ended, suspicion disproven") no later than 90 days after the process was initiated [^src1]. The formal registration period for tracking the number of assessment processes ended due to disproven suspicion began on April 1, 2023, covering the period from April 1, 2023, to March 31, 2024 [^src1].

In the broader context of Danish psychiatric care, the management and registration of these assessment processes are frequently discussed in the ADHD Database's annual and national quality reports. These reports highlight systemic challenges in ADHD quality, including capacity limitations, staff shortages, and the impact of referrals to private actors on data quality. Consequently, strategic revisions of the quality indicators—such as transforming specific indicators into dedicated assessment indicators—are being implemented by the RKKP to improve clinical quality and the overall quality of life for affected children, youth, and adults [^src2].
